result.title: LiquidGazeNet: Towards Event-Based Near-Eye Gaze Estimation under Low-Light Conditions
result.summary: Near-eye gaze estimation under low-light nighttime conditions is challenging because the quality and effective temporal resolution of conventional intensity frames can be reduced. This paper presents LiquidGazeNet, an event-only gaze-estimation framework that combines polarity-aware spike-latency encoding with a custom LTC-based recurrent module. Positive- and negative-polarity events are represented in separate channels, while exponentially decayed time surfaces retain per-pixel temporal recency across successive event windows. A shared convolutional encoder extracts spatial features from each window, and a two-layer recurrent module composed of LTC-inspired cells integrates them causally over short temporal sequences. The network is trained using a hybrid objective that combines screen-space coordinate regression with centre-referenced directional consistency. The framework is evaluated on Gaze-FELL under cross-subject and cross-scene protocols and is further assessed through event-representation, temporal-module, window-duration, and computational ablations. LiquidGazeNet achieves mean errors of 3.75 degrees and 2.41 degrees under cross-subject and cross-scene evaluation, respectively. The results indicate that polarity-aware temporal-recency encoding, together with recurrent integration, is effective for event-only gaze estimation under the evaluated low-light nighttime conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 LiquidGazeNet，用极性分离的事件脉冲延迟编码加指数衰减时间表面表示事件流，并以基于 LTC 的两层循环模块因果整合短时序列，做低光照夜间近眼注视点估计，在 Gaze-FELL 上报告跨被试与跨场景误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 属远领域的注视估计任务，但其「指数衰减时间表面 + 连续时间常数循环状态」可供核查是否能启发 LVR 中 latent 工作区的时序更新与遗忘机制。
